claim: VRC01 broadly neutralizing antibodies target the CD4-binding site of HIV-1 envelope glycoprotein.
source: VRC01 broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) target the CD4-binding site (CD4BS) of the human immunodeficiency virus-1 (HIV-1) envelope glycoprotein (Env).
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is supported by established scientific knowledge about VRC01 antibodies.

claim: VRC01 germline precursors poorly bind to HIV-1 Env.
source: Unlike mature antibodies, corresponding VRC01 germline precursors poorly bind to Env.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and supported by citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: Immunogen design has relied on glycan removal from trimeric Env constructs.
source: Immunogen design has mostly relied on glycan removal from trimeric Env constructs and has had limited success in eliciting mature VRC01 bnAbs.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction and discussion.

claim: VRC01 germline antibodies interacted with a wild-type 426c core lacking variable loops 1–3 in the presence and absence of a glycan at position Asn276.
source: Our results show VRC01 germline antibodies interacted with a wild-type 426c core lacking variable loops 1–3 in the presence and absence of a glycan at position Asn276, with the latter form binding with higher affinity than the former.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data presented in the results section.

claim: 426c core lacking variable loops 1-3 and lacking a glycan at position Asn276 binds VRC01GL with higher affinity than the form containing the Asn276 glycan.
source: Our results show VRC01 germline antibodies interacted with a wild-type 426c core lacking variable loops 1–3 in the presence and absence of a glycan at position Asn276, with the latter form binding with higher affinity than the former.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by BLI data and LC-MS/MS analysis in the results.

claim: Interactions between VRC01GL and 426c core in the presence of an Asn276 oligosaccharide could be enhanced upon carbohydrate shortening.
source: Interactions in the presence of an Asn276 oligosaccharide could be enhanced upon carbohydrate shortening, which should be considered for immunogen design.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by BLI experiments with EndoH-treated samples and kifunensine-treated samples.

claim: HIV-1 Env is a class-I fusion protein responsible for host attachment and fusion of viral and cellular membranes.
source: The HIV-1 envelope (Env) glycoprotein is a class-I fusion protein responsible for host attachment and fusion of the viral and cellular membranes (Dalgleish et al., 1984).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Env trimerizes and undergoes furin-mediated cleavage to yield non-covalent gp120-gp41 pre-fusion trimers.
source: Following expression, Env trimerizes and undergoes furin-mediated cleavage to yield non-covalent gp120-gp41 pre-fusion trimers anchored in the viral membrane (Haim et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: HIV-1 Env is the sole target of neutralizing antibodies.
source: As the sole target of neutralizing antibodies, Env is the focus of intense interest for current vaccine design initiatives.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is established scientific knowledge.

claim: HIV-1 Env relies on multiple mechanisms of immune evasion including dense glycosylation, sequence variation, conformational masking, and presentation of decoy epitopes.
source: However, HIV-1 Env relies on multiple mechanisms of immune evasion – including dense glycosylation, sequence variation, conformational masking, and presentation of decoy epitopes (Burton and Mascola, 2015; Cuevas et al., 2015; Jardine et al., 2015; Kwong et al., 2002; Wei et al., 2003; Zhou et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple citations.

claim: VRC01-class bnAbs derive from the VH1-2 variable heavy chain gene.
source: These bnAbs derive from the VH1-2 variable heavy chain gene (Scheid et al., 2011; Wu et al., 2011), have been isolated from multiple HIV-1-infected patients (Zhou et al., 2013), and putative non-mutated precursors have been identified in naïve individuals (Jardine et al., 2016a).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: VRC01-class bnAbs have been isolated from multiple HIV-1-infected patients.
source: These bnAbs derive from the VH1-2 variable heavy chain gene (Scheid et al., 2011; Wu et al., 2011), have been isolated from multiple HIV-1-infected patients (Zhou et al., 2013), and putative non-mutated precursors have been identified in naïve individuals (Jardine et al., 2016a).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Putative non-mutated precursors of VRC01-class bnAbs have been identified in naïve individuals.
source: These bnAbs derive from the VH1-2 variable heavy chain gene (Scheid et al., 2011; Wu et al., 2011), have been isolated from multiple HIV-1-infected patients (Zhou et al., 2013), and putative non-mutated precursors have been identified in naïve individuals (Jardine et al., 2016a).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: VRC01-class bnAbs are characterized by an unusually short five amino-acid light chain complementary-determining region L3 loop.
source: VRC01-class bnAbs are characterized by an unusually short five amino-acid light chain complementary-determining region (CDR) L3 loop (Zhou et al., 2015) and much higher levels of somatic hyper-mutation than antibodies targeting other pathogens (Wu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: VRC01-class bnAbs have much higher levels of somatic hyper-mutation than antibodies targeting other pathogens.
source: VRC01-class bnAbs are characterized by an unusually short five amino-acid light chain complementary-determining region (CDR) L3 loop (Zhou et al., 2015) and much higher levels of somatic hyper-mutation than antibodies targeting other pathogens (Wu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: VRC01-class bnAbs bind the CD4BS in a way reminiscent of the interactions formed with the viral receptor CD4.
source: They bind the CD4-binding site (CD4BS) in a way reminiscent of the interactions formed with the viral receptor CD4, making extensive CDRH2-mediated contacts while also exhibiting multiple amino acid alterations in the CDRL1 loop relative to germline precursors (Wu et al., 2015; Zhou et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: VRC01-class bnAbs make extensive CDRH2-mediated contacts with the CD4BS.
source: They bind the CD4-binding site (CD4BS) in a way reminiscent of the interactions formed with the viral receptor CD4, making extensive CDRH2-mediated contacts while also exhibiting multiple amino acid alterations in the CDRL1 loop relative to germline precursors (Wu et al., 2015; Zhou et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: VRC01-class bnAbs exhibit multiple amino acid alterations in the CDRL1 loop relative to germline precursors.
source: They bind the CD4-binding site (CD4BS) in a way reminiscent of the interactions formed with the viral receptor CD4, making extensive CDRH2-mediated contacts while also exhibiting multiple amino acid alterations in the CDRL1 loop relative to germline precursors (Wu et al., 2015; Zhou et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: N-linked glycosylation sites surrounding the CD4BS sterically limit recognition by bnAbs.
source: Although N-linked glycosylation sites (NLGSs) that surround the CD4BS sterically limit recognition by bnAbs (Zhou et al., 2017), particularly those present at position Asn276 in Loop D and along the V5 loop, mature VRC01 bnAbs overcome this barrier and potently neutralize numerous HIV-1 viral clades (Zhou et al., 2017; Huang et al., 2016; Stewart-Jones et al., 2016; Wu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Mature VRC01 bnAbs overcome the steric barrier imposed by glycans and potently neutralize numerous HIV-1 viral clades.
source: Although N-linked glycosylation sites (NLGSs) that surround the CD4BS sterically limit recognition by bnAbs (Zhou et al., 2017), particularly those present at position Asn276 in Loop D and along the V5 loop, mature VRC01 bnAbs overcome this barrier and potently neutralize numerous HIV-1 viral clades (Zhou et al., 2017; Huang et al., 2016; Stewart-Jones et al., 2016; Wu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Inferred germline precursors of VRC01-class bnAbs lack detectable binding to trimeric Env constructs harboring glycans at positions Asn276 and V5 loop.
source: In contrast, the inferred germline precursors of VRC01-class bnAbs lack detectable binding to trimeric Env constructs harboring glycans at these locations (Jardine et al., 2013; McGuire et al., 2016; McGuire et al., 2013; Medina-Ramírez et al., 2017b; Stamatatos et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: A trimeric HIV-1 Env protein derived from clade C 426c virus lacking variable loops 1, 2, and 3, and NLGSs at positions Asn276, Asn460, and Asn463 was engineered to bind most VRC01-class precursors.
source: We previously engineered a trimeric HIV-1 Env protein able to bind most VRC01-class precursors (McGuire et al., 2013). This construct was a trimeric gp140 protein derived from the clade C 426c virus and lacked variable loops 1, 2, and 3, along with the putative NLGSs at positions Asn276 (loop D), Asn460, and Asn463 (V5 loop) (McGuire et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: All constructs engineered to engage inferred precursors of VRC01-class bnAbs harbored mutations eliminating NLGSs in loop D at position Asn276 and in the V5 loop.
source: Other constructs have also been engineered to engage the inferred precursors of VRC01-class bnAbs, all of which harbored mutations eliminating the NLGSs in loop D (at position Asn276) and in the V5 loop (Briney et al., 2016; Jardine et al., 2013; McGuire et al., 2016; McGuire et al., 2013; Medina-Ramírez et al., 2017a; Tian et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: A gp120 core derived from the 01dG5 clade virus, which naturally lacks a glycan at position Asn276, engaged the inferred germline precursor of VRC01.
source: Additionally, a gp120 core derived from the 01dG5 clade virus, which naturally lacks a glycan at position Asn276, was also shown to engage the inferred germline precursor of the VRC01 antibody (VRC01GL) (Wu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Glycan-depleted germline-targeting immunogens activate B cells expressing germline VRC01-class BCRs in vivo.
source: Although such glycan-depleted 'germline-targeting' immunogens activate B cells expressing germline VRC01-class BCRs in vivo (Briney et al., 2016; Dosenovic et al., 2015; Tian et al., 2016), they largely fail to elicit mature antibodies capable of bypassing the restrictions imposed by the glycan at position Asn276 (Zhou et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Glycan-depleted germline-targeting immunogens largely fail to elicit mature antibodies capable of bypassing the restrictions imposed by the glycan at position Asn276.
source: Although such glycan-depleted 'germline-targeting' immunogens activate B cells expressing germline VRC01-class BCRs in vivo (Briney et al., 2016; Dosenovic et al., 2015; Tian et al., 2016), they largely fail to elicit mature antibodies capable of bypassing the restrictions imposed by the glycan at position Asn276 (Zhou et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Immunization of rabbits with an engineered clade C Env trimer successfully elicited CD4BS-targeted antibodies distinct from the VRC01 lineage.
source: However, a recent study demonstrated the successful elicitation of CD4BS-targeted antibodies, distinct from the VRC01 lineage, upon immunization of rabbits with an engineered clade C Env trimer (Dubrovskaya et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: VRC01GL Fab has a much lower affinity for 426c DS-SOSIP D3 compared to VRC01GL IgG.
source: The VRC01GL Fab appeared to have a much lower affinity for 426c DS-SOSIP D3, compared to the VRC01GL IgG (the latter bound with an apparent equilibrium dissociation constant of 43 nM (Figure 1B), neglecting the effect of avidity).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by BLI data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: VRC01GL IgG binds 426c DS-SOSIP D3 with an apparent equilibrium dissociation constant of 43 nM.
source: The VRC01GL Fab appeared to have a much lower affinity for 426c DS-SOSIP D3, compared to the VRC01GL IgG (the latter bound with an apparent equilibrium dissociation constant of 43 nM (Figure 1B), neglecting the effect of avidity).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by BLI data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: A cryoEM reconstruction of 426c DS-SOSIP D3†-VRC01GL complex with three bound Fabs was determined at 3.8 Å resolution.
source: This strategy led us to determine two cryoEM reconstructions of the 426c DS-SOSIP D3†-VRC01GL complex (Figure 1D–E, Figure 1—figure supplement 3E–H, Figure 1—figure supplement 4A–D, Figure 1—figure supplement 5): one with three bound Fabs at 3.8 Å resolution (Figure 1D, Table 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 3E, Figure 1—figure supplement 4A–B), and one with two bound Fabs at 4.8 Å resolution (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 3H, Figure 1—figure supplement 4C–D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by cryoEM data shown in figures and Table 1.

claim: A cryoEM reconstruction of 426c DS-SOSIP D3†-VRC01GL complex with two bound Fabs was determined at 4.8 Å resolution.
source: This strategy led us to determine two cryoEM reconstructions of the 426c DS-SOSIP D3†-VRC01GL complex (Figure 1D–E, Figure 1—figure supplement 3E–H, Figure 1—figure supplement 4A–D, Figure 1—figure supplement 5): one with three bound Fabs at 3.8 Å resolution (Figure 1D, Table 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 3E, Figure 1—figure supplement 4A–B), and one with two bound Fabs at 4.8 Å resolution (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 3H, Figure 1—figure supplement 4C–D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by cryoEM data shown in figures.

claim: The 426c DS-SOSIP D3†-VRC01GL V1/V2 apex is closed under cryoEM conditions.
source: Similarly to what was reported for the B41 SOSIP trimer (Ozorowski et al., 2017), the 426c DS-SOSIP D3†-VRC01GL V1/V2 apex is closed under cryoEM conditions (Figure 1D,E,F) whereas it appears open in the conditions we used for negative-staining sample preparation (Ozorowski et al., 2017) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by cryoEM images in Figure 1D, E, F and comparison with negative-staining EM.

claim: The closed 426c DS-SOSIP D3†-VRC01GL trimeric Env conformation lacks a formed gp120 bridging sheet.
source: We note that the closed 426c DS-SOSIP D3†-VRC01GL trimeric Env conformation observed in cryoEM lacks a formed gp120 bridging sheet, which is reminiscent of other closed SOSIP trimer structures (Figure 1G) (Julien et al., 2015; Lyumkis et al., 2013b; Pancera et al., 2014; Stewart-Jones et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 1G and citations.

claim: VRC01GL can bind to a prefusion closed conformation of HIV-1 Env.
source: Our data reveal that VRC01GL could also bind a prefusion closed conformation, which had previously only been reported for its mature counterpart, VRC01MAT (Stewart-Jones et al., 2016) (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by the cryoEM structure and citation.

claim: The 426c DS-SOSIP naturally lacks an NLGS at position Asn234 near the CD4BS.
source: Our structural analysis reveals that the 426c DS-SOSIP naturally lacks an NLGS at position Asn234 near the CD4BS, which is otherwise conserved in 80% of known circulating HIV-1 strains (Crooks et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by structural analysis and citation.

claim: The NLGS at position Asn234 is conserved in 80% of known circulating HIV-1 strains.
source: Our structural analysis reveals that the 426c DS-SOSIP naturally lacks an NLGS at position Asn234 near the CD4BS, which is otherwise conserved in 80% of known circulating HIV-1 strains (Crooks et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a citation.

claim: 426c features a glycan at Asn230 that is more remote from the VRC01 epitope than glycan Asn234.
source: Instead, 426c features a glycan at Asn230 that is more remote from the VRC01 epitope than glycan Asn234 (Jardine et al., 2016b) (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by structural data shown in Figure 1F and citation.

claim: The oligosaccharide at position Asn230 is highly dynamic with only the two proximal N-acetyl-glucosamine moieties resolved in the reconstruction.
source: The oligosaccharide at position Asn230 appears to be highly dynamic, since only the two proximal N-acetyl-glucosamine (GlcNAc) moieties are resolved in the reconstruction (Figure 1—figure supplement 6) and does not interact with VRC01GL or other glycans in the complex.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by structural data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 6.

claim: Glycans at positions Asn276 and Asn234 are in close proximity to each other and likely restrain each others' conformational freedom in clades A and G SOSIP trimers.
source: Previous structural characterization of clades A and G SOSIP trimers established that glycans at positions Asn276 and Asn234 are in close proximity to each other and likely restrain each others' conformational freedom (Jardine et al., 2016b; Stewart-Jones et al., 2016; Zhou et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the results with citations.

claim: The absence of glycan Asn234 in 426c gp120 reduces local carbohydrate crowding near the CD4BS.
source: The absence of glycan Asn234 in 426c gp120 reduces local carbohydrate crowding near the CD4BS which could increase accessibility of this neutralization supersite (Stewart-Jones et al., 2016) and lead to altered local glycan processing (Behrens et al., 2018; Bonomelli et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by inference from structural data and citations.

claim: The 426c DS-SOSIP lacks an NLGS at position Asn362(363).
source: The 426c DS-SOSIP also lacks an NLGS at position Asn362(363), which is present in 42% of strains deposited in the HIV database (Gaschen et al., 2001) (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by structural data shown in Figure 1F and citation.

claim: The NLGS at position Asn362(363) is present in 42% of strains deposited in the HIV database.
source: The 426c DS-SOSIP also lacks an NLGS at position Asn362(363), which is present in 42% of strains deposited in the HIV database (Gaschen et al., 2001) (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a citation.

claim: Fab-bound protomers feature slightly better-resolved density for glycan Asn386 than the free protomer in the asymmetric 426c DS-SOSIP D3†-VRC01GL structure.
source: Analysis of the asymmetric 426c DS-SOSIP D3†-VRC01GL structure, comprising two Fabs, revealed that Fab-bound protomers feature slightly better-resolved density for glycan Asn386 than the free protomer when visualized at the same contour level (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by structural data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: VRC01GL may stabilize the Asn386 glycan through reduction of its conformational freedom and/or via direct interactions with the Fab framework region.
source: These observations suggest that VRC01GL may stabilize the Asn386 glycan either through reduction of its conformational freedom and/or via direct interactions with the Fab framework region.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the structural data.

claim: The absence of glycan Asn362 in 426c gp120 likely contributes to increased accessibility of the CD4BS to VRC01GL-class bnAbs.
source: The absence of glycan Asn362 or other topologically equivalent oligosaccharides in the 426c gp120 sequence likely contributes to increased accessibility of the CD4BS to VRC01GL-class bnAbs due to the close proximity of this glycan to the epitope (Stewart-Jones et al., 2016) (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by inference from structural data and citation.

claim: Glycan Asn197 density is strongest when bound to VRC01GL but appears weaker in the unbound protomer.
source: Similarly to what is observed in available VRC01MAT/SOSIP complex structures (Stewart-Jones et al., 2016), glycan Asn197 density is also strongest when bound to VRC01GL, but appears weaker in the unbound protomer (Figure 1H), again indicating either Fab-induced stabilization or restriction of movement.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by structural data shown in Figure 1H and citation.

claim: The position of glycan Asn197 differs substantially between structures of monomeric gp120 constructs bound to VRC01GL-class Fabs and the VRC01GL-bound SOSIP trimer.
source: The position of glycan Asn197 differs substantially between available structures of monomeric gp120 constructs bound to VRC01GL-class Fabs and the VRC01GL-bound SOSIP trimer reported here (Figure 1G) (Scharf et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 1G and citation.

claim: The variation in Asn197 positioning is guided by the formation of the gp120 bridging sheet in monomeric gp120.
source: This variation in Asn197 positioning is guided by the formation of the gp120 bridging sheet in monomeric gp120, which would otherwise only form following CD4 receptor binding in the context of trimeric Env (Figure 1G) (Kwon et al., 2012; Zhou et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by structural comparison and citations.

claim: The β20/β21 loop orientation in the 426c DS-SOSIP D3†-VRC01GL complex differs relative to crystal structures of VRC01GL-class antibodies in complex with monomeric gp120.
source: This conformational difference includes the β20/β21 loop, whose orientation in the 426c DS-SOSIP D3†-VRC01GL complex differs relative to crystal structures of VRC01GL-class antibodies in complex with monomeric gp120 (Figure 1G) (Scharf et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 1G and citation.

claim: VRC01MAT has minimal preference in the conformation of the bridging sheet or β20/β21 region, as 87% of its contact surface area includes the conformationally invariant outer domain of gp120.
source: Although the β20/β21 loop is close to the VRC01 paratope, VRC01MAT was reported to have minimal preference in the conformation of the bridging sheet or β20/β21 region, as 87% of its contact surface area includes the conformationally invariant outer domain of gp120 (Zhou et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a citation.

claim: VRC01GL in complex with gp120 constructs lacking the bridging sheet domain have been determined, demonstrating that these germline mAbs do not strictly require this region for CD4BS recognition when glycans surrounding the CD4BS are also removed.
source: However, VRC01GL in complex with gp120 constructs lacking this domain have been determined (eOD-GT6 and eOD-GT8), demonstrating that these germline mAbs do not strictly require this region for CD4BS recognition when glycans surrounding the CD4BS are also removed (Jardine et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a citation.

claim: Reintroduction of the NLGS at position Asn460 in the 426c core had no detectable impact on VRC01GL binding affinity.
source: Reintroduction of the NLGS at position Asn460 (S278A/T465A) in the 426c core had no detectable impact on VRC01GL binding affinity despite the predicted overlap of a putative carbohydrate at position Asn460 with the bound VRC01GL Fab (Guo et al., 2012) (Figure 2A–B, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by BLI data shown in Figure 2A-B and Supplementary file 1.

claim: No glycan density could be resolved at position Asn460 in either of the two molecules of the asymmetric unit of the 426c core†-VRC01GL crystal structure.
source: Despite harboring an NLGS, no glycan density could be resolved at position Asn460 in either of the two molecules of the asymmetric unit.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by the crystal structure data.

claim: The Asn460 side chain is hydrogen bonded to the backbone amide and carbonyl groups of the VRC01GL light-chain residue Ile02.
source: Instead, the Asn460 side chain is hydrogen bonded to the backbone amide and carbonyl groups of the VRC01GL light-chain residue, Ile02 (Ile02LC) (Kong et al., 2016)(Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by structural data shown in Figure 2F and citation.

claim: Only unglycosylated Asn460 peptide fragments were detected when analyzing tryptic digests of the 426c core†-VRC01GL sample with LC-MS/MS.
source: In support of this observation, we detected only unglycosylated Asn460 peptide fragments when analyzing tryptic digests of this sample with liquid chromatography coupled to electron transfer/high-energy collision-dissociation tandem mass-spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) (Figure 2H, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by LC-MS/MS data shown in Figure 2H and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Only low levels of glycosylation were detected at Asn460 by qualitative LC-MS/MS analysis of unliganded 426c core.
source: Furthermore, only low levels of glycosylation were detected at Asn460 by qualitative LC-MS/MS analysis of unliganded 426c core (lacking the G459C mutation) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by LC-MS/MS data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: VRC01GL-based immunoprecipitation experiments revealed no difference in glycan occupancy of the Asn460 NLGS between bound and unbound fractions.
source: Additionally, we performed VRC01GL-based immunoprecipitation (IP) experiments utilizing a VRC01GL affinity column and the same 426c core construct. Semi-quantitative LC-MS/MS comparison of the 426c gp120 core samples from fractions that did not bind to VRC01GL ('unbound' flow-through), and those that did ('bound' elution), revealed no difference in glycan occupancy of the Asn460 NLGS (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by LC-MS/MS data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: The Asn460 sequon is rarely glycosylated in 426c core.
source: This indicated this sequon is rarely glycosylated in 426c core and explains its negligible impact on VRC01GL binding.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the LC-MS/MS data.

claim: The predicted overlap of glycan Asn460 with VRC01GL and the absence of a resolved proximal GlcNAc in the crystal structure suggests a likely strict preference for the unglycosylated Asn460 glycoform of the 426c gp120 for binding.
source: The predicted overlap of glycan Asn460 with VRC01GL and the absence of a resolved proximal GlcNAc in the crystal structure of 426c core†-VRC01GL also suggests a likely strict preference for the unglycosylated Asn460 glycoform of the 426c gp120 for binding (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by inference from structural data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Reintroduction of the Asn463 NLGS did not result in a reduction in VRC01GL binding relative to the 426c S278A/T462A/T465A core.
source: We furthermore observed that reintroduction of the Asn463 NLGS (S278A/T462A or S278A) also did not result in a reduction in VRC01GL binding relative to the 426c S278A/T462A/T465A core (Figure 2A,C,D, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by BLI data shown in Figure 2A,C,D and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Electron density for the proximal GlcNAc linked to Asn463 was observed in one of the two molecules of the asymmetric unit of the 426c core†-VRC01GL crystal structure.
source: We observed electron density for the proximal GlcNAc linked to Asn463 in one of the two molecules of the asymmetric unit of the 426c core†-VRC01GL crystal structure and cross-validated the presence of this post-translational modification using LC-MS/MS (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by structural data shown in Figure 2G and LC-MS/MS data.

claim: VRC01GL-based IP experiments followed by semi-quantitative LC-MS/MS detected an Asn463 glycosylation profile which was indistinguishable between bound elution and unbound flow-through fractions.
source: VRC01GL-based IP experiments followed by semi-quantitative LC-MS/MS validated these structural observations by detecting an Asn463 glycosylation profile which was indistinguishable between 'bound' elution and 'unbound' flow-through fractions (Figure 2I).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by LC-MS/MS data shown in Figure 2I.

claim: The Asn463 glycan does not hinder VRC01GL binding in the context of the 426c core and this site is glycosylated.
source: This supports our BLI data suggesting the Asn463 glycan does not hinder VRC01GL binding in the context of the 426c core and that this site is glycosylated.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the BLI and LC-MS/MS data.

claim: VRC01GL bound similarly to both the HEK293F and HEK293 GnTi-/--expressed 426c cores with equilibrium dissociation constants of 11 μM and 15 μM, respectively.
source: BLI analysis revealed VRC01GL bound similarly to both the HEK293F and HEK293 GnTi-/--expressed 426c cores with equilibrium dissociation constants of 11 μM and 15 μM, respectively (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by BLI data shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: The crystal structure of the 426c core†-VRC01GL complex reveals the presence of a resolved glycan at position Asn276 in one of the two molecules of the asymmetric unit.
source: The crystal structure of the disulfide engineered 426c core†-VRC01GL complex expressed in GnTi-/- cells further reveals the presence of a resolved glycan at position Asn276 in one of the two molecules of the asymmetric unit, indicating VRC01GL bound to both Asn276 glycosylated and unglycosylated species (Figure 3C–J).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by structural data shown in Figure 3C-J.

claim: VRC01GL bound to both Asn276 glycosylated and unglycosylated species of 426c core.
source: The crystal structure of the disulfide engineered 426c core†-VRC01GL complex expressed in GnTi-/- cells further reveals the presence of a resolved glycan at position Asn276 in one of the two molecules of the asymmetric unit, indicating VRC01GL bound to both Asn276 glycosylated and unglycosylated species (Figure 3C–J).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by structural data shown in Figure 3C-J.

claim: Distinct sets of interactions are observed between the light chains of VRC01GL or VRC01MAT and glycan Asn276.
source: Analysis of this structure highlights distinct sets of interactions observed between the light chains of VRC01GL or VRC01MAT and glycan Asn276, which is rotated ~90˚ when comparing the two structures (Figure 3C–D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 3C-D.

claim: Asn276 is hydrogen bonded to the VRC01GL light chain residue Tyr91 in the 426c core†-VRC01GL and 426c DS-SOSIP D3†-VRC01GL structures.
source: In line with our previous observation that Asn276 is important for VRC01GL recognition (McGuire et al., 2016), we observed that Asn276 is hydrogen bonded to the VRC01GL light chain residue Tyr91 in our 426c core†-VRC01GL and 426c DS-SOSIP D3†-VRC01GL structures, but not in the JR-FL SOSIP-VRC01MAT crosslinked complex structure (Figure 3C–E) (PDB: 5FYK) (Stewart-Jones et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by structural data shown in Figure 3C-E and citations.

claim: The CDRL1 of VRC01GL accommodates the Asn276 oligosaccharide in a conformation similar to the CDRL1 of unliganded VRC01GL (chain B).
source: Comparisons between the structures of our 426c core†-VRC01GL complex, a putatively authentic germline VRC01/eOD-GT6 complex (PDB ID 4JPK [Jardine et al., 2013]) and the unliganded VRC01GL (PDB ID 4JPI) (Jardine et al., 2013), indicate that the CDRL1 of VRC01GL accommodates the Asn276 oligosaccharide in a conformation similar to the CDRL1 of unliganded VRC01GL (chain B) (Supplementary file 2)(Jardine et al., 2013), but differs from a complex with a gp120 core lacking this glycan (Figure 3F–H).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 3F-H and Supplementary file 2 and citations.

claim: Disulfide crosslinking of 426c core†-VRC01GL did not distort the binding interface into a non-native conformation for the accommodation of glycan Asn276.
source: This observation supports disulfide crosslinking of 426c core†-VRC01GL did not distort the binding interface into a non-native conformation for the accommodation of glycan Asn276 in our structure (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the structural comparison data.

claim: N-linked carbohydrates at position Asn276 of 426c core†-VRC01GL ranged from (GlcNAc)2-(Man)4 to (GlcNAc)2-(Man)5.
source: LC-MS/MS analysis of the sample used for crystallization revealed N-linked carbohydrates at position Asn276 of 426c core†-VRC01GL ranged from (GlcNAc)2-(Man)4 to (GlcNAc)2-(Man)5 (Figure 4A,B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by LC-MS/MS data shown in Figure 4A,B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Unglycosylated Asn276 peptides were identified in the 426c core†-VRC01GL sample used for crystallization.
source: Unglycosylated Asn276 peptides were also identified, corroborating the presence of two populations of molecules in the crystal structure and the ability of VRC01GL to recognize both species (Figure 4A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by LC-MS/MS data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: No (GlcNAc)1 glycopeptides were detected at the Asn276 NLGS by LC-MS/MS despite EndoH treatment of 426c core†-VRC01GL.
source: Despite the EndoH treatment used to promote crystallization of 426c core†-VRC01GL, no (GlcNAc)1 glycopeptides were detected at the Asn276 NLGS by LC-MS/MS (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by LC-MS/MS data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Digested glycopeptides containing (GlcNAc)1 moieties were detected for other NLGSs in 426c core†-VRC01GL, confirming the efficiency of the EndoH treatment.
source: In contrast, we detected digested glycopeptides containing (GlcNAc)1 moieties for other NLGSs, confirming the efficiency of the EndoH treatment (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by LC-MS/MS data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Bound VRC01GL protected the glycan Asn276 from enzymatic digestion by EndoH.
source: These observations validated the Asn276 glycan density observed in the crystal structure and suggested that bound VRC01GL protected the glycan Asn276 from enzymatic digestion (Figure 4A,B), but not other oligosaccharides, such as glycan Asn463 (Figure 2E,G and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by LC-MS/MS data shown in Figure 4A,B and structural data.

claim: EndoH-treated 426c core in the absence of co-expressed VRC01GL contained (GlcNAc)1 moieties at position Asn276.
source: We further corroborated this hypothesis by analyzing EndoH-treated 426c core in the absence of co-expressed VRC01GL and confirmed the presence of (GlcNAc)1 moieties at position Asn276 by LC-MS/MS (Figure 3A,C), supporting that digestion of this glycan was possible if not sterically hindered by the binding of this Fab (Yet et al., 1988).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by LC-MS/MS data shown in Figure 3A,C and citation.

claim: 426c core samples from unbound flow-through and bound elution fractions had distinct migration profiles by SDS-PAGE.
source: To probe whether the disulfide cross-link promoted artificial accommodation of glycan Asn276, we performed an additional analysis with samples obtained from IP experiments using the 426c core construct lacking the G459C mutation. 426c core samples from the 'unbound' flow-through and 'bound' elution fractions had distinct migration profiles by SDS-PAGE (Figure 3I), with the bound fraction exhibiting higher electrophoretic mobility than the unbound species.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by SDS-PAGE data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: The bound fraction from VRC01GL-based IP was enriched for unglycosylated Asn276 peptides.
source: LC-MS/MS revealed the bound fraction was enriched for unglycosylated Asn276 peptides, suggesting this subspecies was the preferred VRC01GL binder (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by LC-MS/MS data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: The majority of the Asn276 peptide signal in bound fractions from VRC01GL-based IP was of the (GlcNAc)2-(Man)5 glycoform.
source: However, we also detected that the majority of the Asn276 peptide signal was of the (GlcNAc)2-(Man)5 glycoform in bound fractions (approximately twice as much as the unglycosylated Asn276 signal) (Figure 3I), suggesting VRC01GL could indeed bind in the presence of this glycan and in the absence of an engineered cross-link.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by LC-MS/MS data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: VRC01GL could bind to a 426c core with wild-type NLGSs in the presence of glycans at positions Asn276 and Asn463.
source: In summary, VRC01GL bound a 426c core with wild-type NLGSs, was sterically compatible with glycans present at positions Asn276 and Asn463, and strictly interacted with a subspecies of gp120 lacking a glycan at position Asn460.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a summary of the findings.

claim: VRC01GL strictly interacted with a subspecies of gp120 lacking a glycan at position Asn460.
source: In summary, VRC01GL bound a 426c core with wild-type NLGSs, was sterically compatible with glycans present at positions Asn276 and Asn463, and strictly interacted with a subspecies of gp120 lacking a glycan at position Asn460.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a summary of the findings.

claim: 426c core expressed using HEK293 GnTI-/- in the absence of kifunensine bound VRC01GL IgG with a KD of 2 µM.
source: The 426c core expressed using HEK293 GnTI-/- in the absence of kifunensine bound VRC01GL IgG with a KD of 2 µM (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, Supplementary file 3), whereas binding was significantly reduced when the 426c core was expressed in the presence of kifunensine (Figure 5C, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by BLI data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and Supplementary file 3.

claim: Binding of VRC01GL IgG to 426c core was significantly reduced when the 426c core was expressed in the presence of kifunensine.
source: The 426c core expressed using HEK293 GnTI-/- in the absence of kifunensine bound VRC01GL IgG with a KD of 2 µM (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, Supplementary file 3), whereas binding was significantly reduced when the 426c core was expressed in the presence of kifunensine (Figure 5C, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by BLI data shown in Figure 5C and Supplementary file 3.

claim: VRC01GL IgG binding affinity to kifunensine-treated 426c core was enhanced following treatment with EndoH (KD = 245 nM).
source: The VRC01GL IgG binding affinity to 426c core expressed in GnTI-/- cells in the presence of kifunensine was enhanced following treatment with EndoH (KD = 245 nM, Figure 5D, Supplementary file 3), confirming recognition of gp120 by VRC01GL IgGs can occur in the presence of a proximal GlcNAc at position Asn276.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by BLI data shown in Figure 5D and Supplementary file 3.

claim: Recognition of gp120 by VRC01GL IgGs can occur in the presence of a proximal GlcNAc at position Asn276.
source: The VRC01GL IgG binding affinity to 426c core expressed in GnTI-/- cells in the presence of kifunensine was enhanced following treatment with EndoH (KD = 245 nM, Figure 5D, Supplementary file 3), confirming recognition of gp120 by VRC01GL IgGs can occur in the presence of a proximal GlcNAc at position Asn276.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by BLI data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: VRC01GL-based IP and subsequent semi-quantitative LC-MS/MS of the 426c core expressed in the absence of kifunensine revealed a consistent preference for short and/or unglycosylated species bound to VRC01GL.
source: In line with these hypotheses, the VRC01GL-based IP and subsequent semi-quantitative LC-MS/MS of the 426c core expressed in the absence of kifunensine revealed a consistent preference for short and/or unglycosylated species bound to VRC01GL (Figure 3I, Figure 5F,G,H,I).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by LC-MS/MS data shown in Figure 3I and Figure 5F,G,H,I.

claim: The Asn276 oligosaccharide is expected to have a pronounced negative effect on VRC01GL binding due to its direct overlap with the VRC01GL epitope.
source: While many 426c core glycans are likely to be affected by either kifunensine or EndoH treatment, the Asn276 oligosaccharide is expected to have a pronounced negative effect on VRC01GL binding due to its direct overlap with the VRC01GL epitope (Stewart-Jones et al., 2016; Zhou et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by inference from structural data and citations.

claim: The 426c core†-VRC01GL crystal structure does not resolve ordered mannose rings at position Asn276, and only the two proximal GlcNAc moieties were modeled.
source: The 426c core†-VRC01GL crystal structure does not resolve ordered mannose rings at position Asn276, despite their high detected abundance by LC-MS/MS, and thus only the two proximal GlcNAc moieties were modeled in our structure (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by structural data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The Asn276 mannose moieties are likely not directly involved in binding to VRC01GL light chain, but rather act as a steric barrier VRC01GL must overcome to interact with the CD4BS.
source: This indicates the Asn276 mannose moieties are likely not directly involved in binding to VRC01GL light chain, but rather act as a steric barrier VRC01GL must overcome to interact with the CD4BS.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the structural data.

claim: Qualitative LC-MS/MS analyses of the 426c DS-SOSIP trimer revealed longer glycans at the Asn276 NLGS, which correlated with a poorer binding affinity relative to the 426c core.
source: Qualitative LC-MS/MS analyses of the 426c DS-SOSIP trimer, expressed in the absence of kifunensine, revealed longer glycans at the Asn276 NLGS, which correlated with a poorer binding affinity, relative to the 426c core also expressed in the absence of kifunensine (Figure 1A, Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by LC-MS/MS data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2 and BLI data in Figure 1A.

claim: The increased affinity of VRC01GL for the 426c core following digestion with EndoH indicates VRC01GL-specificity and compatibility for proximal GlcNAcs.
source: VRC01GL-specificity and compatibility for proximal GlcNAcs is made evident by the increased affinity of VRC01GL for the 426c core following digestion with EndoH (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by BLI data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Binding of several germline antibodies to gp120 core constructs could potentially be modulated by tailoring protein expression conditions, oligosaccharide length, and/or by endoglycosidase treatment.
source: These results indicate binding of several germline antibodies to gp120 core constructs could potentially be modulated by tailoring protein expression conditions, oligosaccharide length, and/or by endoglycosidase treatment, as opposed to strict mutations aimed at abolishing NLGSs (Kong et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the findings with a citation.

claim: 82% of sequenced HIV-1 clades harbor a threonine residue at position 278 of gp120.
source: Whereas 82% of sequenced HIV-1 clades harbor a threonine residue at position 278 of gp120, 426c gp120 contains a serine at this position.
evidence: This is stated in the results and is based on sequence analysis.

claim: 426c gp120 contains a serine at position 278.
source: Whereas 82% of sequenced HIV-1 clades harbor a threonine residue at position 278 of gp120, 426c gp120 contains a serine at this position.
evidence: This is stated in the results and is based on sequence analysis.

claim: NXT NLGS sites are more efficiently glycosylated relative to NXS sites.
source: Since recent reports suggested NXT NLGS sites are more efficiently glycosylated relative to NXS sites (Huang et al., 2017), we compared the binding kinetics of full-length VRC01GL-class IgGs, VRC01GL and 12A21GL, to HEK293 GnTI-/--expressed 426c core and an 426c S278T core mutant (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a citation.

claim: The S278T mutation reduced the equilibrium dissociation constant by 10-fold relative to the wild type NLGS, mainly by decreasing association kinetics.
source: BLI experiments demonstrated the S278T mutation reduced the equilibrium dissociation constant by 10-fold relative to the wild type NLGS, mainly by decreasing association kinetics (Figure 6A–D, Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by BLI data shown in Figure 6A-D and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The S278T mutation did not abrogate VRC01GL-class antibody binding.
source: The S278T mutation did not abrogate VRC01GL-class antibody binding, despite an expected improvement in Asn276 glycosylation efficiency (Huang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by BLI data and citation.

claim: Semi-quantitative LC-MS/MS revealed (GlcNAc)2-(Man)5 oligosaccharides were predominantly detected at position Asn276 in the S278T mutant.
source: Moreover, semi-quantitative LC-MS/MS revealed (GlcNAc)2-(Man)5 oligosaccharides were predominantly detected at position Asn276 in the S278T mutant, though some unglycosylated peptides were still present at low levels (Figure 5A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1H,I).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by LC-MS/MS data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1H,I.

claim: No appreciable difference in affinities was detected among NLGS-depleted 426c core mutants S278A, S278V, and S278R.
source: Although the magnitude of binding was improved relative to both 426c core constructs containing a glycan at position Asn276, no appreciable difference in affinities was detected among any of these NLGS-depleted 426c core mutants (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by BLI data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-F.

claim: A significant fraction of the interactions observed by BLI between the 426c core (containing an intact Asn276 NXS NLGS) and VRC01GL occurred with the unglycosylated Asn276 subspecies.
source: Since binding was reduced following introduction of the S278T mutation, these results collectively suggest that a significant fraction of the interactions observed by BLI between the 426c core (containing an intact Asn276 NXS NLGS) and VRC01GL occurred with the unglycosylated Asn276 subspecies.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the BLI data.

claim: VRC01GL-class IgG binding was detected with the 426c S278T core.
source: However, VRC01GL-class IgG binding was also detected with the 426c S278T core (Figure 6A–D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), and EndoH treatment (which retains core GlcNAcs) of both the S278 and S278T constructs significantly improved IgG binding relative to their untreated counterparts (Figure 6E–H, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by BLI data shown in Figure 6A-D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: EndoH treatment of both the S278 and S278T constructs significantly improved IgG binding relative to their untreated counterparts.
source: However, VRC01GL-class IgG binding was also detected with the 426c S278T core (Figure 6A–D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), and EndoH treatment (which retains core GlcNAcs) of both the S278 and S278T constructs significantly improved IgG binding relative to their untreated counterparts (Figure 6E–H, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by BLI data shown in Figure 6E-H and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: VRC01GL-class binding is dampened by the Asn276 mannose moieties.
source: Although these findings support that VRC01GL-class binding is dampened by the Asn276 mannose moieties , interactions were still possible, as underscored by the presence of this carbohydrate in the crystal structure (Figure 3C), the EndoH protection assay (Figure 4B,C), and VRC01GL-based IP LC-MS/MS analyses of non-crosslinked samples (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by structural data, EndoH protection assay, and LC-MS/MS data.

claim: The ability of VRC01GL-class antibodies to recognize a CD4BS containing an NLGS at position Asn276 and the linked oligosaccharide is unprecedented.
source: The ability of VRC01GL-class antibodies to recognize a CD4BS containing an NLGS at position Asn276 and the linked oligosaccharide is unprecedented, and highlights a potentially unique feature of the 426c core construct containing all native NLGSs for engagement of VRC01GL antibodies.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: Mature VRC01-class bnAbs are produced only in a small fraction of infected individuals and only after up to a decade following the initial infection.
source: However, mature VRC01-class bnAbs are produced only in a small fraction of infected individuals and only after up to a decade following the initial infection (Wu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation.

claim: VRC01GL bound to the deglycosylated 426c DS-SOSIP D3† trimer in the absence of a formed bridging sheet.
source: Using this crosslinking strategy, we demonstrated that VRC01GL bound to the deglycosylated 426c DS-SOSIP D3† trimer in the absence of a formed bridging sheet and that this binding stabilized surrounding CD4BS carbohydrates at position Asn197 and Asn386.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of findings.

claim: VRC01GL binding stabilized surrounding CD4BS carbohydrates at position Asn197 and Asn386.
source: Using this crosslinking strategy, we demonstrated that VRC01GL bound to the deglycosylated 426c DS-SOSIP D3† trimer in the absence of a formed bridging sheet and that this binding stabilized surrounding CD4BS carbohydrates at position Asn197 and Asn386.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of findings.

claim: The absence of glycans at positions Asn234 and Asn362 in 426c likely enhanced accessibility of the CD4BS to bnAbs and could affect processing of nearby carbohydrates.
source: Considering there was a minor enrichment for the unglycosylated Asn197 glycoform in 'bound' fractions following VRC01GL-based immunoprecipitation of the 426c core, there could be an entropic cost associated with binding in the presence of this particular oligosaccharide. Additionally, we found that 426c naturally lacks glycans at positions Asn234 and Asn362, which likely enhanced accessibility of the CD4BS to bnAbs and could affect processing of nearby carbohydrates (Behrens et al., 2018), including glycan Asn276.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by inference from data and citation.

claim: The absence of glycans at positions Asn234 and Asn362 is one of the reasons explaining the ability of 426c DS-SOSIP D3 and 426c core constructs to bind VRC01GL-class antibodies.
source: We propose this is one of the reasons explaining the ability of 426c DS-SOSIP D3 and 426c core constructs to bind VRC01GL-class antibodies.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: Immunogen design efforts focusing on VRC01-class bnAbs have largely relied on the mutagenic removal of NLGSs during priming followed by their reinsertion during subsequent boosts.
source: Immunogen design efforts focusing on VRC01-class bnAbs have thus far largely relied on the mutagenic removal of NLGSs during priming followed by their reinsertion during subsequent boosts (McGuire et al., 2013; Medina-Ramírez et al., 2017a; Zhou et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations.

claim: The complete absence of NLGSs during the priming phase may remove a selection pressure guiding proper accommodation of these glycans during antibody affinity maturation.
source: The complete absence of these NLGSs during the priming phase may also remove a selection pressure guiding proper accommodation of these glycans during antibody affinity maturation, and could explain the limited success achieved thus far to elicit VRC01-class bnAbs capable of neutralizing natively glycosylated wild-type viruses.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation about the implications of the findings.

claim: Alternative priming and boost strategies retaining native NLGSs may need to be considered.
source: As a result, alternative priming and boost strategies retaining these native NLGSs may need to be considered.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a recommendation based on the findings.

claim: HIV-1 gp120 core constructs have differential processing of NLGSs around the CD4BS relative to their trimeric SOSIP counterparts.
source: Specifically, HIV-1 gp120 core constructs have previously been shown to have differential processing of NLGSs around the CD4BS relative to their trimeric SOSIP counterparts (Bonomelli et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation.

claim: Reintroduction of 426c gp120 V5 loop NLGSs did not negatively impact VRC01GL binding to the 426c core in contrast with what was detected for trimeric 426c gp140.
source: We observed that reintroduction of 426c gp120 V5 loop NLGSs did not negatively impact VRC01GL binding to the 426c core in contrast with what was detected for trimeric 426c gp140 (McGuire et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data and citation.

claim: VRC01GL Fabs and IgGs could bind to the 426c core (containing a wild-type Asn276 NLGS) but not to a trimeric 426c DS-SOSIP construct containing all wild-type NLGSs.
source: We found that VRC01GL Fabs and IgGs could bind to the 426c core (containing a wild-type Asn276 NLGS) but, as expected, not to a trimeric 426c DS-SOSIP construct containing all wild-type NLGSs (Huang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data and citation.

claim: The interaction between VRC01GL and 426c core is likely permitted in part due to the absence of variable loops 1, 2, and 3, and could potentially be further augmented by the natural absence of glycans at position Asn234 and Asn362.
source: We put forward this interaction is likely permitted in the 426c core in part due to the absence of variable loops 1, 2, and 3, and could potentially be further augmented by the natural absence of glycans at position Asn234 and Asn362.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: Stabilized trimeric pre-fusion closed SOSIP constructs may impart additional negative steric effects not present in the monomeric gp120 core.
source: It is also possible that stabilized trimeric pre-fusion closed SOSIP constructs impart additional negative steric effects not present in the monomeric gp120 core.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation.

claim: There is a reduced amount of trimming of the Asn276 glycan in the 426c DS-SOSIP trimer relative to the 426c core monomer.
source: This is supported by our observation that there is a reduced amount of trimming of the Asn276 glycan in the 426c DS-SOSIP trimer relative to the 426c core monomer.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data.

claim: The reduced trimming of the Asn276 glycan in the 426c DS-SOSIP trimer could arise from steric properties of the trimer which would be absent in soluble monomeric constructs, thereby limiting unfettered access of the glycosylation machinery to this site during expression.
source: This could arise from steric properties of the trimer which would be absent in soluble monomeric constructs, thereby limiting unfettered access of the glycosylation machinery to this site during expression.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation about the mechanism.

claim: VRC01GL binding to 426c core constructs preferentially occurred using expression systems allowing for production of short glycans.
source: We found that VRC01GL binding to 426c core constructs preferentially occurred using expression systems allowing for production of short glycans and provided a structural framework for accommodation of the Asn276 oligosaccharide by the VRC01GL CDRL1.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of findings.

claim: The unglycosylated Asn276 variant is the preferred VRC01GL binding partner.
source: As is the case for VRC01MAT (Jardine et al., 2013; McGuire et al., 2016; McGuire et al., 2013; Medina-Ramírez et al., 2017a; Stamatatos et al., 2017), we would like to emphasize that the unglycosylated Asn276 variant is the preferred VRC01GL binding partner and likely had an important contribution to the interactions observed by BLI.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data and citations.

claim: Accommodation of the Asn276 oligosaccharide could occur during VRC01GL binding in the absence of CDRL1 loop shortening and/or glycine addition.
source: However, we detected glycosylation at position Asn276, both structurally and by LC-MS/MS following VRC01GL-based IP experiments, in the VRC01GL-bound fractions, in the presence and absence of cysteine cross-linking, respectively. This indicated accommodation of this oligosaccharide could occur during VRC01GL binding in the absence of CDRL1 loop shortening and/or glycine addition, arguing in favor of its retention in epitope-based constructs derived from the 426c strain of HIV-1.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data.

claim: VRC01GL binding to a 426c core is possible and appears to occur both in the absence and presence of a glycan at position Asn276.
source: The structural and biophysical data reported here provide a foundation for understanding how bnAbs targeting the HIV-1 CD4BS may be elicited in humans in the presence of a native Asn276 NLGS. We demonstrated structurally that VRC01GL binding to a 426c core is possible and appears to occur both in the absence and presence of a glycan at position Asn276, supporting recently proposed hypotheses (Jardine et al., 2016b; Scharf et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of findings and supported by data and citations.

claim: Introduction of an NXS NLGS at position Asn276 of gp120 core constructs lacking selected variable loops and in absence of glycans Asn234, Asn362(363), and Asn460 could prove a useful strategy to elicit VRC01-class antibodies during the priming phase of immunization.
source: Introduction of an NXS NLGS at position Asn276 of g120 core constructs lacking selected variable loops and in absence of glycans Asn234, Asn362(363), and Asn460 could prove a useful strategy to elicit VRC01-class antibodies during the priming phase of immunization.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a recommendation based on the findings.

claim: Germline-targeting vaccine design strategies starting with a gp120 immunogen may be a promising alternative to current priming strategies focusing on glycan-depleted HIV-1 SOSIP trimers.
source: Additionally, the stark differences in binding observed between VRC01GL and 426c DS-SOSIP or 426c core constructs suggests 'germline-targeting' vaccine design strategies starting with a gp120 immunogen may be a promising alternative to current priming strategies focusing on glycan-depleted HIV-1 SOSIP trimers.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a recommendation based on the findings.

claim: The use of insect cell expression systems may further benefit recognition of the HIV-1 CD4BS due to the abundance of paucimannose sugars.
source: In the context of VRC01GL-targeted immunogens, the use of insect cell expression systems may further benefit recognition of the HIV-1 CD4BS due to the abundance of paucimannose sugars (Altmann et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation with a citation.

claim: The use of insect cell expression systems has been reported to enhance the immunogenicity of the CD4BS for other HIV-1 antibodies, but has yet to be specifically shown for antibodies of the VRC01 lineage.
source: This approach has already been reported to enhance the immunogenicity of the CD4BS for other HIV-1 antibodies, but has yet to be specifically shown for antibodies of the VRC01 lineage (Kong et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation.

claim: The crystal structure of 426c core†-VRC01GL was determined at 2.3 Å resolution.
source: We co-expressed these proteins using HEK293 GnTI-/- cells, which lack N-acetyl-glucosaminyltransferase I activity and thus are unable to generate complex N-linked carbohydrates (Wright and Morrison, 1994). We then determined its crystal structure at 2.3 Å resolution after endoglycosidase H (EndoH) treatment to facilitate crystallization (Depetris et al., 2012; Freeze and Kranz, 2010) (Figure 2E, Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by crystallographic data shown in Table 2.
